Hi Elaine — thanks for the list. Attached is a draft SOW and a throughput model we ran against your Q4 batch profile (attachments). Quick answers inline:

1) Pool mapping — yes. We propose two reserved pools: PH-Clinical (6x A100-equivalent GPUs) and PH-Search (4x A100-equivalent GPUs). Each pool is isolated at the routing layer and billed to the same commitment.

2) Tokens/sec guarantee — we propose a baseline SLO of 85,000 tokens/sec for PH-Clinical and 45,000 tokens/sec for PH-Search measured as a 5-minute rolling average. For burst windows we include a 3-minute tiered buffer that allows up to 1.5x baseline for up to 30 minutes/day. See spreadsheet for simulation numbers.

3) Remedies — our standard approach for Reserved Pool Throughput Addenda: service credits tied to the percent of minutes below SLO in a billing month. We define minimum measurement windows, exclusion events (scheduled maintenance, force majeure), and a remediation runway (30-day ops plan) before credits apply. Draft language is in the SOW addendum.

Next steps: if this looks directionally correct, I'll route the addendum to Legal/Procurement and send a DocuSign. If Marcus wants a technical runbook for failover (routing to burst-capacity or degraded-model fallback), we can include that as an appendix.

Hi Marcus — quick answers and scheduling:

- SLO measurement is aggregate at the reserved-pool level (tokens/sec per pool). We translate LB concurrency into expected tokens/sec using a conversion table (tokens per request median). We'll include that table in the SOW appendix so your throttles map to pool-level SLOs.
- Burst allowance is a daily budget per pool but unused minutes roll into a 7-day carryover window (so not strictly single-day only). Spillovers between pools are allowed only when both pools are on the same commitment and routed with a shared-burst policy — we'll surface the policy choices in the addendum.

I've scheduled an ops sync with our SRE (Rishi) for Sep 29 at 10:00 PT; calendar invite sent. Prepare the sample traffic trace if you can.

Marissa

Subject: Re: Renewal: Capacity top-up + reserved throughput SLO execution plan

Hi team — follow-up from today's runbook review. Per Marcus's ask, here's the technical commitments we'll include in the final addendum:

- Pool sizing: PH-Clinical = 6x A100-equivalent; PH-Search = 4x A100-equivalent. GPUs are pinned to the pool; we guarantee isolation of inference memory and KV cache to avoid noisy neighbors.
- Measurement: tokens/sec measured as 1-minute averages reported to both parties via an SLO dashboard (Redwood Console link). Monthly SLO compliance = percentage of minutes in calendar month where pool >= baseline tokens/sec.
- Burst policy: each pool gets 30 minutes/day at up to 1.5x baseline; unused minutes roll forward up to 7 days; shared-burst permitted when both pools under same commitment and enabled by customer.
- Credits: service credit tiering: <99% monthly compliance -> 10% credits on that month's committed invoice portion; <95% -> 25% credit. Credits are the exclusive financial remedy; escalation path includes 48-hour incident review and a 30-day remediation plan.
- Failover: automatic routing to a compatible quantized model group in a separate Dedicated pool if capacity is exhausted; this is accompanied by a decline in max tokens/sec but preserves tail latency.

Attached: a short ops appendix and final SOW snippet (we'll push PDF/DocuSign once legal has reviewed).

Thanks,
